lessons.title: Company identity and history
objectives: Explain AITS using supported public facts.
explanation: The official About us page identifies A.I.T.S. Company Limited and dates its founding to Buddhist year 2548, equivalent to 2005. It describes a business concerned with installation quality and professional service. These are public company statements; they do not establish an employee contract or a field acceptance standard.

The public mission text emphasizes service standards, technology, attention to customer needs and responsibility. In this course, these themes introduce the business. Specific targets, individual duties and performance measures require current approved internal documents. Do not infer a reporting line or an employee benefit from marketing language.
lessons.example: A fictional new colleague asks whether the company began in 2548 or 2005. Explain the calendar conversion and identify the company page as the source.
lessons.exercise: Write a two-sentence company introduction and name one fact that still requires internal confirmation.
lessons.model_response: AITS publicly dates its founding to 2005 and describes IT and security installation services. My reporting manager must be confirmed from current internal records.
key_points: Service quality and responsibility are public themes

lessons.title: Services and customer needs
objectives: Match customer needs to relevant service categories.
explanation: AITS publicly lists CCTV, network cabling, security systems, internet, telephone systems, access control, home automation and solar services. Learn what each category addresses before proposing a product. CCTV supports visual monitoring; access control manages entry; network infrastructure connects devices and services.

A customer request may span several categories. Ask about the problem, location, existing equipment and desired outcome. Record uncertainty instead of promising compatibility, price, installation dates or a service level. A technical survey and approved quotation process are separate from this introductory training.
lessons.example: Fictional Lotus Workshop wants to see its entrance remotely and restrict staff-door access. CCTV and access control are relevant; connectivity also needs investigation.
lessons.exercise: List three discovery questions for Lotus Workshop without collecting passwords.
lessons.model_response: What areas need coverage? Who should be allowed through the door? What network equipment and connection already exist?

lessons.title: Roles and collaboration
objectives: Prepare a clear handover without inventing an organization chart.
explanation: No current approved AITS organization chart was located in the inspected materials. This lesson therefore describes functions, not confirmed departments or reporting lines. In a typical service business, customer-facing staff capture requirements, technical staff assess feasibility, administration maintains records, and an authorized reviewer confirms commercial or operational decisions.

A useful handover states the request, known facts, open questions, relevant evidence and next action. It identifies who is being asked to respond without assuming authority they do not have. Ask your supervisor to confirm actual role names and escalation routes. A handover is incomplete when the recipient cannot tell what decision is needed.
lessons.example: Synthetic ticket LH-001 says “camera problem.” A better handover says “Entrance camera image missing since 09:00; other views work; model and safe observations attached; technical diagnosis requested.”
lessons.exercise: Rewrite “customer unhappy, please fix” as a five-field handover.
lessons.model_response: Request: restore entrance view. Facts: missing since 09:00. Evidence: authorized screenshot without people. Unknown: power status. Next action: technical review and agreed update time.
key_points: Functional map is not an organization chart
lessons.thai_summary: แผนภาพในบทเรียนเป็นตัวอย่างการประสานงาน ไม่ใช่ผังองค์กรที่อนุมัติ ต้องยืนยันช่องทางส่งต่อกับบริษัท
lessons.summary: Functional map is not an organization chart Facts and unknowns travel together Confirm the real escalation route

lessons.title: Learning Hub and your first learning cycle
objectives: Complete a lesson, attempt a quiz and distinguish practice from approval.
explanation: Open the Learning Hub with your assigned account, select an assigned course and read the lesson objectives. Work through the explanation and exercise before taking the quiz. Review feedback, revisit the relevant lesson and retry when the platform permits. A recorded completion shows learning activity; it does not authorize electrical work or certify job competence.

The knowledge library separates approved records from clearly labeled samples. Check title, version, source, approval state and applicability before using a document. Course publication and knowledge approval are separate controls. If internal policy is unavailable, ask HR or your supervisor for the current approved document. AI practice cannot supply missing company authority.
lessons.example: A sample checklist appears in the library. You may use it for the exercise, but should not treat it as permission to perform a live installation.
lessons.exercise: Open one course, complete its first lesson, locate its source note and identify its approval label.
lessons.model_response: Record the course and lesson IDs, the visible Draft/sample label and the source reference; confirm completion persists after reopening.
key_points: Read and practise before the quiz
